body:
Priya Raman: Jamal, thanks for making time. I know as a founder your time is precious. Should we jump right in?

Jamal Osei: Please. I've got twenty-five minutes before my next thing.

Priya Raman: Perfect. Tell me about Anchorline. You've got, what, thirty trucks on the road?

Jamal Osei: Forty-two now as of last week. We do last-mile freight for e-commerce brands in the Pacific Northwest. Our customer support is mostly drivers calling in — dispatch questions, delivery exceptions, that sort of thing. We're also fielding some end-consumer calls from brands whose customers got our number instead of the brand's number.

Marcus Fields: How many inbound calls a day?

Jamal Osei: About two hundred and twenty. Averaging three minutes. My ops manager is drowning and I can't justify hiring another full-time support person yet.

Priya Raman: Got it. And what would success look like for you?

Jamal Osei: Anything that takes the driver calls off my ops manager's plate. Driver calls are super repetitive — where's my dispatch, what's the customer address, that kind of thing. Consumer calls I want a human touch on because those are our brand partners' customers.

Marcus Fields: That's a totally reasonable split. We can build a driver-only bot on our startup tier and route consumer calls straight to your ops manager.

Jamal Osei: Alright, hit me with pricing. What am I looking at?

Priya Raman: Startup tier is nine cents per minute with a floor of two thousand a month. For your volume — two-twenty calls a day at three minutes, so roughly nineteen thousand eight hundred minutes a month — you'd land right at the floor, two thousand a month. Twenty-four a year.

Jamal Osei: Two grand a month. Okay. That is more than I was hoping for, to be honest. I was budgeting fifteen hundred.

Priya Raman: I hear you. The floor is a hard-ish number but let me ask — if we did a six-month pilot at fifteen hundred a month with a step-up to two thousand after the pilot, would that work?

Jamal Osei: That would work. What do I lose at the pilot rate?

Priya Raman: You'd be on shared infrastructure, so during peak periods you might see slightly higher latency — talking maybe two hundred milliseconds worse than the standard tier. And you don't get the dedicated Slack channel with our support team, you'd go through the shared community channel.

Jamal Osei: I can live with that for six months.

Marcus Fields: Jamal, what telephony are you on today?

Jamal Osei: We're on a small provider called Voxbone — I think they're owned by Bandwidth now. Standard SIP.

Marcus Fields: Standard SIP is fine. We can integrate.

Jamal Osei: How fast can we go live?

Marcus Fields: For driver-only intents with your volume, honestly three to four weeks. It's a small intent set.

Jamal Osei: Alright. Send me the pilot proposal. I want to be up in April.

Priya Raman: I'll have it to you by end of week.

Jamal Osei: One more thing — what happens if we grow? We're on track to double our fleet in the next twelve months.

Priya Raman: The pilot rate holds through the six months regardless of volume. If you exceed thirty thousand minutes we'd revisit for the standard-tier transition.

Jamal Osei: Fair.

Marcus Fields: Also — as you scale, we can build out more intents. Driver payroll questions, load-board integration, that sort of thing.

Jamal Osei: Yeah, payroll questions come up a lot. Every Friday afternoon.

Marcus Fields: We can absolutely handle that. We'd want a read-only connection to your payroll system — do you use Gusto, ADP, something else?

Jamal Osei: Gusto.

Marcus Fields: We have a Gusto connector. Read-only, so no risk of us modifying anything.

Jamal Osei: Good.

Priya Raman: What about reporting — do you need anything specific?

Jamal Osei: Just a weekly digest to my ops manager. Nothing fancy.

Priya Raman: That's built in. You'll set it up during onboarding.

Jamal Osei: Perfect. Alright, gotta jump.

Marcus Fields: One quick question — SMS follow-ups. Do you use them today?

Jamal Osei: Yeah, our dispatch system sends drivers SMS updates.

Marcus Fields: Good to know. We can plug into that flow too if useful.

Jamal Osei: Let's revisit that in the pilot. Great. Gotta jump, thanks folks.

Priya Raman: Thanks Jamal.
